- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.70) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >35.0), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops sharply after a peak), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day moving average.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.30) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply smoothing or lag correction to first 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.70, -0.30, +0.70), model tends to overfit recent sentiment; use sentiment-weighted average instead of pure trend-following.
